name: Joda
overview: Joda is a male figure mentioned in the genealogy of the Messiah as recorded in Luke 3:26. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he holds significance for being part of the ancestral line leading to Jesus Christ. There are no additional notes about his life or character beyond this genealogical placement.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Joda' appears as a proper name in Luke 3:26. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is indicated in the Scriptures, so it is presented plainly as an ancestral name within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Joda is the son of Josech, as inferred from Luke 3:26, and the father of Joanan, explicitly stated in Luke 3:27. These relationships place him clearly within a family line important to the Messianic genealogy.
scriptureSignificance: Joda's significance rests primarily in his role within the lineage of the promised Messiah, Jesus Christ. His mention in the Gospel of Luke underscores the fulfillment of God's covenant through a continuous, divinely ordained family line. Although not a prominent character in narrative events, his inclusion affirms the historical and theological foundation of Christ's human ancestry.
